info.text: English for Aviation Maintenance · Unit 15 — MEL dispatch with the duty engineer. Listening, reading, use of English and vocabulary. CEFR B2.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Which air-conditioning pack is inoperative?

generalfeedback.text: Kārlis reports that the number two pack is inoperative; the flow-control valve fails to open.

feedback.text: Correct — the number two pack.
No — number one keeps working; number two is the fault.
No — only one pack fails, which is why dispatch is possible.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The MEL lets the flight climb above FL310 with one pack inoperative.

generalfeedback.text: False. A single pack cannot pressurise the cabin above FL310, so the flight level must not exceed it.

feedback.text: No — FL310 is the limit, not a level to climb past.
Correct — the flight must stay at or below FL310.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many calendar days is the rectification interval for the category C pack item? (Write the number.)

generalfeedback.text: A category C item gives a ten-day rectification interval.

feedback.text: Correct — ten calendar days.
No — three days is a category B item, like the APU.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The single-pack altitude limitation is flight level ___. (Write the number, e.g. 310.)

generalfeedback.text: The limitation is FL310 — three one zero, as read on the call.

feedback.text: Correct — FL310.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. Which document covers the missing static wick?

generalfeedback.text: A missing part is not an MEL item. It goes to the configuration deviation list (CDL).

feedback.text: Correct — the configuration deviation list.
No — the MEL covers inoperative systems, not a missing part.
No — the load sheet is about weight and balance.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. The 737 has a second weather radar as a backup.

generalfeedback.text: False. Inga says there is only one radar, so there is no backup.

feedback.text: No — there is only one radar on this aircraft.
Correct — no second radar; that is why the proviso matters.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. How many start attempts did the crew make on the APU? (Write the number.)

generalfeedback.text: The crew tried three starts with no light-up.

feedback.text: Correct — three attempts.
No — listen again; it was more than two.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. Is the inoperative APU automatically a no-go item?

generalfeedback.text: No — the engineer reads the MEL first. With a ground air source it becomes a go item.

feedback.text: Correct — the provisos decide, not the fault alone.

answer.text: It is always a no-go item.

feedback.text: No — a met proviso makes it a go item.

answer.text: It can never be deferred here.

feedback.text: No — it is deferred for three days under category B.

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL note.

MEL 33-42-01 · Landing light (one). Repair category C — rectification interval 10 calendar days. Number installed: 2. Number required: 1. One landing light may be inoperative provided the affected light is placarded and, for a night departure, the crew is briefed.

How many landing lights must work for dispatch?

generalfeedback.text: Two are installed but only one is required for dispatch.

feedback.text: Correct — number required for dispatch is 1.
No — two are installed, but only one is required.
No — at least one must work.

questiontext.text: Read the MEL note in R1 again. The inoperative landing light must be placarded before dispatch.

generalfeedback.text: True. The proviso requires the affected light to be placarded.

feedback.text: Correct — the proviso requires a placard.
No — read the proviso: the light must be placarded.

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

Repair categories set the rectification interval: category A has an interval stated in a note; category B is 3 calendar days; category C is 10 calendar days; category D is 120 calendar days.

An item is category B. How long is the rectification interval?

generalfeedback.text: Category B is a three-day interval.

feedback.text: Correct — category B is 3 calendar days.
No — ten days is category C.
No — that is closer to category D (120 days).

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

Sign the certificate of release to service only after the placard is fitted and both the maintenance (M) and operational (O) procedures are complete.

You may sign the release before fitting the placard.

generalfeedback.text: False. The release is signed only after the placard is on and both procedures are done.

feedback.text: No — the placard and both procedures come first.
Correct — placard and procedures first, then sign.

name.text: U15 R5 — MEL vs CDL text

questiontext.text:
Read this note.

The MEL covers systems and equipment that are inoperative. The configuration deviation list (CDL) covers secondary parts that are missing, such as a static wick or an access panel.

An access panel is missing from the airframe. Which document applies?

generalfeedback.text: A missing part is a CDL matter, not an MEL matter.

feedback.text: Correct — the CDL covers missing secondary parts.
No — the MEL is for inoperative systems, not missing parts.
No — that document is about mass and balance.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite with a modal. It is not permitted to climb above FL310.
The flight ______ climb above FL310. (Two words.)

generalfeedback.text: A firm prohibition is must not + the bare verb.

feedback.text: Correct — must not climb.
Correct — the contracted form.
Use "must not" — a strong prohibition, no "to".

questiontext.text:
Rewrite for the future. We are able to fix it now.
Tomorrow we ______ fix it. (Four words; not a double modal.)

generalfeedback.text: You cannot say "will can". Future ability is will be able to.

feedback.text: Correct — will be able to fix it.
No — modals never stack. Use "will be able to".
The answer is "will be able to".

questiontext.text:
Complete for a physical impossibility.
A single pack ______ pressurise the cabin above FL310. (One word.)

generalfeedback.text: Impossibility uses cannot (or can't).

feedback.text: Correct — cannot pressurise.
Correct — the contracted form.
Use "cannot" — it is not physically possible.

questiontext.text:
Name the term. The time limit to repair a deferred item.
The ______ ______. (Two words.)

generalfeedback.text: The rectification interval — ten days for category C, three for B.

feedback.text: Correct — the rectification interval.
The term is "rectification interval".

questiontext.text:
Rewrite with a modal. The aircraft is allowed to dispatch with one pack out.
The aircraft ______ dispatch with one pack out. (One word.)

generalfeedback.text: Permission granted by the MEL is may (or can) + bare verb.

feedback.text: Correct — may dispatch.
Also correct — can dispatch.
No — never "to" after a modal. Just "may".
Use "may" or "can".

questiontext.text:
Name the term. A small warning label fitted near a broken control.
A ______. (One word.)

generalfeedback.text: A placard — you fit an "INOP" placard by the switch.

feedback.text: Correct — a placard.
No — "placate" is a different word. The label is a placard.
The term is "placard".

name.text: U15 U7 — fix the modal error

questiontext.text:
Correct the error. The aircraft may to dispatch tonight.
The aircraft ______ tonight. (Two words.)

generalfeedback.text: Drop the "to": a modal takes the bare verb, so may dispatch.

feedback.text: Correct — may dispatch, no "to".
No — remove "to" after the modal.
The answer is "may dispatch".

questiontext.text: Match each MEL term to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: Proviso = a condition to meet; limitation = a limit on the flight; no-go item = a fault that stops dispatch; serviceable = fit for use.

answer.text: a condition you must meet to dispatch
a limit on the flight, such as an altitude

questiontext.text: Match each document to what it records.

generalfeedback.text: The MEL lists inoperative items; the CDL lists missing parts; the tech log records faults and actions; the CRS is the signed release.

answer.text: which inoperative items still allow flight
which missing parts still allow flight
the running record of faults and actions
the signed statement the aircraft is safe

questiontext.text: Which verb fits: "The rectification interval ______ in three days"?

generalfeedback.text: An interval expires. After that, the item must be fixed or the aircraft is grounded.

feedback.text: Correct — the interval expires.
No — aircraft depart; intervals expire.
No — that is about leaving a job.

questiontext.text: Which verb fits: "______ the deferred defect in the technical log"?

generalfeedback.text: You raise a deferred defect in the tech log — the standard collocation.

feedback.text: Correct — raise the deferred defect.
No — you do not launch a defect entry.
No — that has nothing to do with a log entry.
